pos.personaBrief: Cruyff held that dominating the ball means the opponent cannot score ('if you play in possession you don't have to defend'), and Barcelona moved the ball constantly to unbalance blocks.

pro.personaBrief: Barcelona built from the keeper with short passes and a ball-playing pivot (Guardiola), accepting risk under pressure, with the ball 'moved and moved'.

est.personaBrief: Positional 3-4-3 with defined roles and rondo-based close combinations, plus a false nine dropping to link with midfielders.

lar.personaBrief: Cruyff widened the pitch with two wingers and advancing full-backs, so width was central to his system, though wingers also moved inside.

blo.personaBrief: Compact block with a high defensive line (a defender pushed forward) and strikers as first defenders, but the sources say his teams rarely counter-pressed intensely.

mar.personaBrief: Marking scheme is not documented; the compact block and space-based organisation suggest zonal, and he left corner defending to the keeper.

pla.personaBrief: He imposed his model at Ajax and Barcelona (sold 15 players), told players to concentrate on themselves and not the opponent, and kept attacking against Milan in 1994.

res.personaBrief: He preferred winning 5-4 to 1-0, told players to 'go out and enjoy it', and stayed attacking even when it cost him (1994 final).

sis.personaBrief: A strong collective model where every position has duties (striker first defender, goalkeeper first attacker), turning youngsters into key players, with technical freedom inside it.

jog.personaBrief: Technique took precedence over physical condition in training; he picked short, technical players over aerial ones.

bas.personaBrief: Gave debuts to Bergkamp and promoted Guardiola ('good enough is old enough'), valued La Masia and youth, while also buying core signings.

lid.personaBrief: Dominant boss who told the president not to enter his dressing room and sold mutineers, applied his own rules, and clashed with Stoichkov; not a consensus builder.
